section_summary.extract_value: This section describes a single study of college women: 143 initially consented, with exclusions (32 for too few surveys, 15 for timing, 4 for outlying BMIs) yielding a final sample of 92 females. Mean age was 19.7 (SD = 1.93); ethnic breakdown included 50% Caucasian. BMI (self-reported) ranged 15.6–35 with mean 22.62 (SD = 3.41). No measures of body appreciation or correlations with BMI are reported in this section.
section_summary.evidence_source: One-hundred and forty-three college women consented to participate in the study. Ofthese, 32 completed three or fewer surveys, and so were removed because we feltthey provided too few assessment points to allow for an adequate examination of within-person fluctuations. An additional 15 participants were removed because they failed to complete their surveys during the required time frames, and another four were removed because they had outlying BMIs (over 40). Our final sample consisted of 92 females. Mean age in the sample was 19.7 (SD = 1.93) and the ethnic breakdown was: 50% Caucasian, 21% East Asian, 1.6% Southeast Asian, 4.8% Black/African, 9.7% South Asian, 1.6% Middle Eastern, 1.6% West Indian/Caribbean, 1.6% Aboriginal, and 8.1% unknown. BMI, calculated based on self-reported weight and height (kg/m2), ranged from 15.6 to 35 in the sample, with a mean of 22.62 (SD = 3.41).
